content.comment_body: Hello, can someone explain the practical difference between using network input addresses and memory markers for network access? In one of my projects, network input addresses (e.g. [article_no]) were used for the lights, while memory markers (e.g. [article_no]) were used for the rollers. I am currently working with [product_name] [version_no] together with Node-RED and node-red-contrib-s7. Thank you.

Hi [user_name], With [product_name], there is a specified address range (0-850) enabling read and write operations via network to and from VM memory using the program. Additionally, external devices can directly access the status of inputs and outputs (including over the network). You can also operate flags and outputs directly if they are not managed by a program in [product_name]. A list of available addresses is provided in the documentation. Best regards, [user_name] (translated with Google)

Network inputs refer to designated network input addresses, while flags are internal memory markers. Only the project's author can explain why network inputs were chosen in some cases and markers in others. For more details on VM addresses, refer to the online help.

The VM region of [product_name] can be accessed by compatible devices or applications as DB1. Examples: M1 = [article_no] in [product_name], and for compatible devices/apps: [article_no]. MB0 (M1-M8) = [article_no] in [product_name], and for compatible devices/apps: [article_no]. NAI1 = [article_no] in [product_name], and for compatible devices/apps: [article_no].
